original_question.stem:
Match each case in List-I with the appropriate assessment in List-II. Use only the information stated in each case.

List-I
(A) An old scanner is no longer used because a newly invented scanner has replaced it.
(B) A printer is no longer used because it broke; no new device replaced it.
(C) An older radio remains in regular use, although a newer radio has been invented.
(D) A new audio player has just been invented; no earlier player is said to have stopped being used because of it.

List-II
(I) Both the end of use and the new invention as its cause are stated.
(II) The item is still in use.
(III) The item is no longer used, but a new invention is not given as the cause.
(IV) A new invention is mentioned, but no earlier item is said to have stopped being used because of it.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

original_question.stem:
Arrange the following sentences in a coherent order.
(A) Only after this match was confirmed did he open it and count the notebooks inside.
(B) He then recorded that number on the receipt and placed the notebooks in the cupboard.
(C) Before opening the parcel, Ravi compared its address with the class's order receipt.
(D) Ravi received a sealed parcel addressed to his class.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

items.original_explanation: Sentence (D) introduces the parcel, and (C) describes checking its address against the receipt before opening it. In (A), “this match” refers to that check, after which Ravi opens the parcel and counts the notebooks. Sentence (B) refers to the resulting count, so the coherent order is (D), (C), (A), (B).

reasons: failed:source_support
failed:source_support
D introduces Ravi receiving the parcel; C gives the address check before opening; A says opening and counting occur only after the match is confirmed; B records the count and puts the notebooks away.
The supplied source describes these events in the same order, supporting D, C, A, B.
source_support.syllabus_topic: Rearranging parts: ordering sentences into a coherent sequence

original_question.stem: What choice do the children make after the neighbour questions whether the new game must reproduce the old one?
options: They stop drawing because their memories conflict.
They use the first child's remembered layout.
They create a changed layout instead of copying the old one.
They recreate the old arrangement exactly from memory.
original_question.passage: Rain had washed the chalk game from the lane. The children arrived with fresh chalk and began drawing again. One child remembered the old squares as longer; another insisted that the turning square had been on the left. They argued until a passing neighbour asked whether the new game had to reproduce the old one. After a moment, they drew a wider turning square in the middle. Their feet soon covered the fresh lines with pale dust. From her doorway, the neighbour could no longer tell which marks belonged to yesterday and which belonged to the game they had just invented.
